qt: to the Commission Benoit Cassart (Renew) Subject:

The entry into force of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation on 12 August 2026 is imposing a crippling administrative burden on businesses, especially SMEs. Due to the lack of clarity caused by the delay in the explanatory guidelines and lack of implementing acts, economic operators are having to move ahead without any direction. This situation directly penalises honest entrepreneurs, undermining our SMEs and e-commerce. Given the current technical uncertainty and the fact that some implementing acts are not yet operational, does the Commission intend to ask the Member States to relax the transition conditions by granting an official moratorium on penalties in order to protect our companies, in particular our SMEs?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.10.2026)

The Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation1 (PPWR) contributes to the better functioning of the Single Market by harmonising national measures on packaging and packaging waste in order to avoid obstacles to trade and the distortion and restriction of competition within the EU. It also contributes to the transition to a circular economy, reducing dependencies on virgin raw materials, improving resource security and supporting more resilient value chains. The PPWR provides time to adapt, as well as exemptions, simplified requirements and other provisions to reduce burdens on smaller businesses. The timeline for the implementing legislation is set in the PPWR and lays down a staged approach. The Commission has proposed in its Environmental Omnibus proposal2 to suspend the obligation for producers to appoint an authorised representative when they conduct direct sale to end users in other Member States. Such suspension will immediately alleviate a significant burden for EU producers3. The Commission has called upon the European Parliament and the Council to adopt the proposal as quickly as possible and stands ready to work on it as a matter of urgency. In the meantime, the Commission recommended to Member States – based on the provisions of the PPWR – to take a constructive and pragmatic approach and to avoid disproportionate enforcement. The Commission will continue to work closely with the Member States and stakeholders to support a pragmatic implementation of the PPWR.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging

and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025. 2 https://circulareconomy.europa.eu/platform/en/news-and-events/all-news/environmental-omnibus-has-beenpublished. 3 Especially Small and Medium-sized Enterprises.
